title: Destination-therapy solid-organ xenotransplantation

concept.text: Destination-therapy solid-organ xenotransplantation would use an engineered animal organ as a durable replacement for a failing human organ. A gene-edited pig kidney, heart or liver would sustain the recipient’s life over years, with an acceptable treatment burden, rather than serve only as a temporary bridge to a human donor organ. Human procedures have demonstrated that pig organs can provide clinically meaningful function, but the supplied evidence does not establish this durable replacement capability.

Conceptual synthesis: the innovation combines transplant surgery with animal genome engineering, immune management, physiological compatibility, infection surveillance and reliable donor-animal production. Its defining achievement would be reproducible long-term replacement of a particular organ’s function. Destination therapy describes the intended durable clinical role; it does not require a guarantee of lifelong graft survival, freedom from immunosuppression or proof of zero infection risk.

significance.text: The revolutionary possibility is a new source of life-sustaining organs that can be produced rather than obtained solely through human donation. Organ shortage remains a major constraint on transplantation, and demonstrated human kidney and heart xenograft function provides a technical basis for pursuing this additional supply. If durable performance becomes reproducible, engineered pigs could substantially expand the pool of transplantable organs.

Conditional impact synthesis: reliable production, suitable recipient eligibility and clinical access could allow more planned operations and reduce dependence on unpredictable human donor offers. Kidney recipients might gain sustained freedom from dialysis; successful heart or liver replacement could offer another treatment route when existing support is inadequate. Fewer waiting-list deaths and less time spent on bridging treatment are plausible downstream benefits, but graft survival alone would not establish them. They require favorable comparative outcomes and delivery of organs to patients who can benefit.

Limits of the supply analogy: describing xenotransplantation as an industrial supply change captures the possibility of breeding and preparing donor animals, but does not establish organs available on demand. Production capacity, consistency, pathogen control, surgical capacity, cost and access would constrain the practical effect. Immunosuppression-free treatment, lifelong function and elimination of zoonotic risk would be additional advances beyond useful destination therapy. Success with one organ type would not establish equivalent success with other solid organs.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central missing capability is reproducible multi-year organ function in living recipients despite the immune response across species. Edited pig organs have avoided hyperacute rejection in reported human procedures, but this early success does not prevent subsequent antibody-mediated rejection, T-cell-mediated rejection or innate immune activation. The October 2026 Nature review reports immune-mediated injury in most procedures described to that point.

Delayed injury is a particularly important barrier. The supplied review’s account of a kidney that supported 271 dialysis-free days traces early T-cell-mediated rejection through later injury to small vessels and their endothelial lining, progressing to thrombotic microangiopathy. This shows why initial function and treatment of an early rejection episode cannot establish durable compatibility. The original assertion that this injury occurred despite a negative crossmatch is not verified by the retained evidence and cannot be used to draw conclusions about crossmatch performance.

Engineering synthesis: a destination graft must also maintain the recipient’s required physiology and interact acceptably with human blood and coagulation over prolonged use. Immune control must remain effective without imposing an intolerable burden from treatment or infection. The supplied clinical accounts establish persistent immune injury, but do not fully characterize or resolve this combined physiological, coagulation and long-term treatment problem. These are requirements to investigate, rather than a claim that every component has already failed in every recipient.

Translation synthesis: sustained infection surveillance and reproducible donor-organ quality must accompany clinical durability. The engineering challenge includes both the organ and the system that produces, screens, implants and monitors it. Kidney, heart and liver programs need separate evidence because their physiological demands, failure modes and available rescue treatments differ.

current_state.text: Kawai and colleagues’ report, published online on 7 February 2025, describes a 62-year-old man who received a porcine kidney with 69 genomic edits. The kidney functioned immediately and dialysis stopped. T-cell-mediated rejection on day 8 was reversed with intensified immunosuppression. The recipient died from unexpected sudden cardiac causes on day 52; autopsy showed severe coronary artery disease and ventricular scarring without evident xenograft rejection. The retained abstract supports this clinical course, but does not state the transplant year or explicitly identify the procedure site. The earlier attribution to a 2024 procedure at Massachusetts General Hospital is therefore not established by that abstract.

A separate living-recipient kidney course achieved 271 days without dialysis, according to an annotated reference in the Nature review published on 21 October 2026. That secondary account describes early T-cell-mediated rejection followed by late microvascular injury and thrombotic microangiopathy. It supplies evidence for prolonged bridge function even though the underlying Lancet report was not captured in the supplied source collection.

The earlier account of that 271-day course also stated that the graft was removed, immunosuppression was reduced because of infection, the crossmatch remained negative, surveillance detected no zoonotic infection, and the recipient subsequently received a human kidney. Those details cannot be verified from the retained secondary account because the primary Lancet text is absent. Their evidentiary limitation does not show that they are false, but they cannot be treated here as established case findings.

For hearts, a 2025 Circulation review reports two living recipients treated through expanded access who survived 40 and 60 days, with xenograft failure preceding death in both. The separate Nature Medicine report published online on 8 January 2025 describes a 58-year-old recipient of a heart with 10 gene edits. Near-complete loss of systolic function required extracorporeal membrane oxygenation on day 31, and the recipient transitioned to comfort care after 40 days. These reports demonstrate temporary life-supporting function and substantial failure risk, without establishing destination therapy. The supplied Griffith abstract is complete; the earlier description of it as truncated was incorrect.

A 61-day kidney xenotransplant experiment in a brain-dead decedent documented immune injury despite treatment, including combined antibody-mediated and cell-mediated rejection at postoperative day 49. The multi-omics paper was published online on 13 November 2025, with its version of record and issue appearing in 2026. This experiment contributes evidence about rejection mechanisms over an extended observation period, but cannot establish long-term recovery, treatment tolerability or survival in a living recipient.

The two Nature documents available to the supplied review were subscription previews containing abstracts and additional material such as references or figure captions, rather than complete main texts and methods. A four-page supplementary PDF associated with the decedent study yielded no usable scientific text, so it adds no verified support here. These access and extraction limits constrain interpretation of mechanisms and case details; they do not negate the results supported by the retained passages.

Taken together, the supplied reports demonstrate human xenograft function lasting days to months, including a secondary account of 271 dialysis-free days, alongside persistent immune barriers. They do not demonstrate reproducible multi-year destination therapy. No corresponding durable living-recipient liver series is established by these inputs. The supplied freshness record does not establish comprehensive coverage through 1 November 2026, so this conclusion concerns the available evidence rather than an exhaustive claim about every procedure performed by that date.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: conduct prospective series of gene-edited pig kidneys and at least one life-supporting heart or liver series, using prespecified organ-specific comparisons with contemporary deceased-donor transplantation at one and three years. Define recipient populations, sample sizes, acceptable performance margins and analysis methods in advance. These durations and the inclusion of more than one organ type are proposed thresholds for a convincing demonstration, not established clinical standards.
completion_criteria.label: Kidney and heart-or-liver series report prespecified one- and three-year comparisons

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical endpoints: measure patient survival, graft survival, organ function, hospital discharge and sustained freedom from dialysis or mechanical support required because of graft failure. Report rejection episodes, rescue treatment, infection, treatment burden and quality of life. A claim that outcomes resemble human transplantation would require appropriate comparison populations and explicit margins, rather than an informal comparison of selected survivors.
completion_criteria.label: Clinical outcomes and treatment burden reported with appropriate comparisons

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and safety requirements: demonstrate comparable results across recipients, donor-animal cohorts and clinical teams, while documenting the genetic configuration, production conditions and immune regimen used. Systematic porcine-pathogen surveillance should specify which agents are sought, test sensitivity, sampling schedules and follow-up duration. No detected clinically significant transmission would support safety within those observation limits; it would not establish zero zoonotic risk.
completion_criteria.label: Comparable results reproduced across cohorts and teams with pathogen surveillance

completion_criteria.text: Proposed benefit and supply tests: where feasible, a later randomized comparison against continued dialysis or waiting-list care could assess clinical benefit. Production volumes, organ suitability, delivery times, cost and equitable clinical access would separately test whether xenotransplantation expands usable supply. A finite series would establish demonstrated breadth within its studied organs, recipients and follow-up, without proving permanent function for every recipient or universal applicability across solid organs.
completion_criteria.label: Clinical benefit and usable supply assessed within demonstrated limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis — SUR-01, Operational donor-specific tolerance for the transplants patients actually receive: both concepts confront immune injury and the burden of chronic immunosuppression. Tolerance could improve the durability and usability of a xenograft if it can be achieved across species. The concepts remain distinct: SUR-01 concerns immune acceptance, whereas SUR-02 concerns durable organ replacement from an animal source. Useful destination xenotransplantation could still require ongoing immunosuppression.

Roster-based synthesis — SUR-12, Life-sustaining autologous solid organs assembled for implantation: both would address organ scarcity by creating an additional organ source. SUR-12 proposes organs assembled from an autologous source; SUR-02 uses engineered animal organs and must manage compatibility across species. Only the SUR-12 title and the earlier high-level comparison were supplied, so a detailed comparison of methods, maturity or achievable immune advantages is not established.

Roster-based synthesis — SUR-03, Life-sustaining cryobanking of human-scale organs: cryobanking could complement xenotransplantation by helping separate organ production or procurement from implantation time. Its central challenge is preserving and restoring a usable organ, whereas SUR-02 must establish durable function and compatibility after implantation. Storage success would not itself solve xenograft rejection, and xenograft success would not establish successful cryobanking.

Roster-based synthesis — SUR-09, Living, perfused autologous replacements for complex parts that grafts do not supply: both involve replacing living tissue and maintaining perfusion and integration. SUR-09 addresses complex parts using an autologous route, while SUR-02 addresses life-sustaining solid organs from animals. Shared surgical and vascular challenges do not make these the same innovation.

Roster-based synthesis — SUR-11, Real-time cellular and molecular vision of the intact operative field: improved sensing could potentially assist assessment of organ condition or injury, but the roster supplies no evidence of such an application to xenotransplantation. Diagnostic visibility would be an enabling capability; it would not itself establish durable xenograft function.

change_log.change: Preserved SUR-02 and its destination-therapy identity while defining the goal as reproducible durable replacement.
change_log.reason: The concept remains coherent even though individual supporting assertions require qualification; the supplied evidence does not establish its achievement.

change_log.change: Separated expanded organ supply from on-demand availability, planned operations and reduced waiting-list mortality.
change_log.reason: The latter outcomes additionally require production capacity, clinical access and favorable comparative outcomes.

change_log.change: Reclassified immunosuppression-free treatment, lifelong graft function and elimination of zoonotic risk as additional ambitions.
change_log.reason: They are not necessary conditions for clinically useful destination therapy.

change_log.change: Retained the supported immune barriers and late microvascular injury while qualifying the negative-crossmatch assertion.
change_log.reason: The October 2026 review supports the injury sequence but does not verify the crossmatch detail.

change_log.change: Preserved the 271-day dialysis-free result with explicit secondary attribution.
change_log.reason: The retained Nature review independently supports that duration despite the absent Lancet primary text.

change_log.change: Identified graft removal, infection-triggered immunosuppression reduction, zoonotic surveillance findings and subsequent human transplantation as unverified case details.
change_log.reason: These assertions are not established by the retained secondary material; missing evidence is not a contradiction.

change_log.change: Preserved the 69-edit kidney course but did not assert the original transplant year or hospital as verified.
change_log.reason: The retained Kawai abstract supports the clinical findings without specifying those procedural details.

change_log.change: Integrated the detailed heart failure course and corrected the claim that the Griffith abstract was truncated.
change_log.reason: The complete retained abstract supports mechanical support from day 31 and transition to comfort care after 40 days.

change_log.change: Clarified the decedent study’s publication chronology and included its supported combined rejection finding at day 49.
change_log.reason: Online publication occurred in November 2025, with the version of record and issue in 2026; the retained review supports the day-49 finding.

change_log.change: Expanded completion criteria to include patient survival, treatment burden, prespecified comparisons, reproducibility and surveillance sensitivity.
change_log.reason: These additions make the proposed demonstration clinically interpretable without presenting its thresholds as consensus standards.

change_log.change: Separated clinical benefit testing from production and access testing, and limited conclusions to the organs and populations studied.
change_log.reason: A clinical comparison alone cannot establish a supply effect, and finite demonstrations cannot establish universal applicability.

change_log.change: Integrated source-access, extraction and freshness limitations and added qualified roster comparisons.
change_log.reason: The final record must distinguish supported findings from unavailable detail and conceptual overlap from verified technical equivalence.

unresolved_issues: The uncaptured Lancet report is needed to verify graft removal, infection-related immunosuppression reduction, negative crossmatch, zoonotic surveillance findings and subsequent human transplantation in the 271-day kidney course.
The supplied Kawai abstract does not verify the original claim that the procedure occurred in 2024 at Massachusetts General Hospital.
The supplied freshness record does not establish comprehensive coverage through 2026-11-01.
Subscription-preview access limits assessment of the Nature papers’ full methods and analyses; the supplementary PDF’s scientific content cannot be established from its text extraction.
The proposed trials still require justified sample sizes, organ-specific performance margins, comparison populations and pathogen-surveillance specifications.
The evidence does not determine which donor edits and immune regimens can deliver reproducible multi-year function with an acceptable treatment burden for each organ type.
Production scalability, cost, recipient eligibility and access remain separate questions from graft durability.
Detailed overlap assessments are limited because the related concepts were supplied as roster titles rather than full records.

brief.title: Pig organs that replace failing human organs for years
possible: People with organ failure could receive a pig kidney, heart or liver whose genes have been changed to help it work in a human body. The organ would support life for years, with a manageable treatment burden, rather than temporarily support someone awaiting a human donor.

Kidney recipients could stay off dialysis, the treatment that filters blood when kidneys fail. People with heart or liver failure could gain another treatment option when existing support is inadequate.
why: Organs could come from animals bred for donation, expanding supply beyond human donors. More patients could receive transplants, and operations could be planned with less dependence on unpredictable donor offers.

sources.showed: A pig kidney immediately worked well enough for a patient to stop dialysis. Treatment reversed an immune attack on the organ, and kidney function continued until the patient died from sudden cardiac causes.
sources.quote: The patient's creatinine levels decreased promptly and progressively, and dialysis was no longer needed.
sources.cited_for: A pig kidney can replace enough kidney function to stop dialysis in a living person.
sources.not_established: A single patient's course does not establish reliable function over years.

sources.showed: This is a study of a pig kidney used as temporary support before a human kidney transplant.
sources.cited_for: It concerns prolonged temporary kidney replacement.
sources.not_established: Temporary support does not establish durable replacement over years.

sources.showed: A genetically modified pig heart initially pumped and relaxed well in a living recipient. It later failed, requiring mechanical support.
sources.quote: The xenograft initially functioned well, with excellent systolic and diastolic function during the first several weeks posttransplantation.
sources.cited_for: A pig heart can temporarily sustain a living recipient.
sources.not_established: The heart failed within weeks, and this single case does not establish durable replacement.

sources.showed: Their review describes living recipients whose pig hearts supported them temporarily but failed before death. Immune barriers persisted despite progress against immediate rejection.
sources.quote: with xenograft failure preceding death in both cases.
sources.cited_for: Human heart transplants from pigs have provided temporary function with substantial failure risk.
sources.not_established: These cases do not establish sustained survival or dependable heart replacement.

sources.who: Raphael P. H. Meier and colleagues
sources.showed: Their review reports that immune injury remains common after pig-organ transplantation. It also describes a kidney recipient who spent 271 days without dialysis before later small-vessel injury.
sources.quote: However, these major advances also brought new challenges into focus, as immune-mediated graft injuries including antibody-mediated rejection, T cell-mediated rejection and innate immune activation have been observed in most xenotransplantation procedures to date.
sources.cited_for: Months of useful function can coexist with delayed immune injury.
sources.not_established: The review does not establish a treatment that reliably prevents late organ damage.

sources.showed: They tracked immune activity in a pig kidney transplanted into a brain-dead recipient. They found several forms of immune attack and tissue injury despite treatment.
sources.quote: There was also evidence of interactions between activated pig-resident macrophages and infiltrating human immune cells.
sources.cited_for: Immune injury involves interacting human and pig cells and remains a barrier after gene changes.
sources.not_established: A brain-dead recipient cannot establish long-term survival, recovery or treatment tolerability in living patients.

shown: Pig kidneys and hearts have supported living people for days to months. A review by Meier and colleagues describes a kidney recipient who went 271 days without dialysis, followed by injury to small blood vessels. This is prolonged useful function, but lasting replacement remains unproven.
missing: Repeated success would have to establish organ function lasting years in living recipients.
Immune control would have to prevent delayed damage with tolerable treatment and infection risks.
Organs would have to meet human physiological needs and interact reliably with human blood over prolonged use.
Consistent donor-organ quality and sustained monitoring for pig infections would have to accompany clinical success.

milestones.label: Kidney and heart or liver comparisons through three years
milestones.explanation: Planned kidney studies and a heart or liver series would compare outcomes with deceased-donor transplants at prespecified follow-ups. This would test durability against agreed standards for each organ.

milestones.label: Patient outcomes and treatment burden meet agreed comparisons
milestones.explanation: Studies would compare survival, organ function, discharge, freedom from support, rejection, infection and quality of life in suitable patient groups. This would establish whether useful function comes with an acceptable treatment burden.

milestones.label: Results repeat across patients, donor groups and clinical teams
milestones.explanation: Comparable outcomes would recur across patients, donor-animal groups and teams, with documented gene changes, care and systematic infection monitoring. This would test reliability and safety within the observation limits.

milestones.label: Patient benefit and usable organ supply are demonstrated
milestones.explanation: Later trials would compare benefit with dialysis or waiting-list care where feasible, while supply assessments measured production, suitability, delivery, cost and access. This would test whether more patients could receive useful treatment.

uncertain: Which gene changes and immune treatments can sustain each organ type for years with an acceptable treatment burden remains unknown.
Study sizes, comparison groups, acceptable outcome differences and infection-monitoring rules still need justification.
Production scale, cost and fair access remain separate questions from whether the organs last.

page.title: Destination-therapy solid-organ xenotransplantation
page.definition: A genetically engineered pig organ replaces the function of a failed human kidney, heart or liver as ongoing treatment. Xenotransplantation means transplantation between species. In destination therapy the pig organ is intended to sustain the recipient without a planned human transplant. An auxiliary liver graft can provide temporary support while the patient awaits recovery or a human liver.

goal.need: On 30 July 2026, US waiting lists had 95,492 entries for a kidney, 8,776 for a liver and 4,039 for a heart. Some kidney candidates face years on dialysis and may die waiting. Pig donors could make transplantation possible when a suitable human organ is unavailable. For a kidney recipient, lasting graft function could mean years free from dialysis. Recipients would still need monitoring for infections that can pass from pigs to people.

completion.title: FDA licenses a pig organ for ongoing replacement of failed human organ function.
completion.criterion: FDA approves a biologics licence application for a genetically engineered pig organ with an indication for ongoing replacement of human organ function in end-stage disease. Approval covers the organ product and its manufacturing facilities under Public Health Service Act section 351. An indication limited to temporary support pending recovery or human transplantation does not establish destination therapy. Achievement is assessed separately for each organ type.
completion.set_by: FDA, applying Public Health Service Act section 351(a)(2)(C) and its biologics licensing framework.
completion.threshold_quote: the biological product that is the subject of the application is safe, pure, and potent;
completion.basis: FDA requires a biologics licence for marketing a xenotransplantation product. EXPAND and EXPRESS identify a BLA as their registration pathway. Licensure assesses a specified product, indication and manufacturing system. United Therapeutics' filing on 4 November 2026 describes its xenografts as development-stage products. The published framework supplies no common multi-year survival cutoff.

milestones.title: Pig grafts show consistent, long-term function in an animal model relevant to the intended use.
milestones.criterion: Prospectively assess long-term graft survival and safety in a series of animals using the intended clinical product and, where feasible, the clinical immunosuppression regimen and surgical procedure. Demonstrate stable, reproducible graft function. For hearts, ISHLT specifies at least 5–10 nonhuman primate models across multiple centres, each showing at least 6 months of survival with normal graft function on stable maintenance immunosuppression. FDA individualises the preclinical programme for each product.
milestones.set_by: FDA describes the general design of definitive preclinical studies in its 2022 briefing document. ISHLT sets the numerical cardiac benchmark in its 2026 consensus perspective.
milestones.threshold_quote: at least 5–10 non-human primate models across multiple centers, each demonstrating ≥6 months of survival

milestones.title: A pig organ provides life-supporting function in a living human.
milestones.criterion: Document an interval in which the transplanted organ supplies the function a living recipient needs. For a kidney, demonstrate renal function sufficient for independence from dialysis. For a heart, demonstrate circulation sustained by the graft without mechanical circulatory support. For a liver, demonstrate that the graft supplies the required hepatic function independently of the native liver. Record the duration of support.
milestones.set_by: Clinical proof-of-concept convention. IXA identifies dialysis independence for kidneys and freedom from mechanical support for hearts, and distinguishes auxiliary liver support from definitive replacement.
milestones.threshold_quote: These cases clearly demonstrated life-supporting pig heart function in both patients;

milestones.title: FDA permits a prospective clinical trial of a pig organ to proceed under an effective IND.
milestones.criterion: The investigational new drug application covering the prospective trial goes into effect 30 days after FDA receives it unless FDA notifies the sponsor of a clinical hold, or on earlier FDA notification that the clinical investigations may begin.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 312.40. The cited programme authorisations concern kidney and heart transplantation.
milestones.threshold_quote: An investigator may not administer an investigational new drug to human subjects until the IND goes into effect

milestones.title: A prospective trial completes its protocol-defined safety and efficacy assessment in the cohort.
milestones.criterion: Account for the trial cohort through the protocol’s assessment point, including deaths and graft failures. EXPAND and EXTEND assess kidney recipients at 24 weeks, and EXPRESS assesses heart recipients at 24 weeks. The ChoironeX kidney protocol measures adverse events through Month 6 and recipient survival without chronic dialysis at Month 6. Assess each organ under its own protocol. These time points specify when outcomes are measured.
milestones.set_by: Sponsor-defined endpoints in EXPAND, EXTEND, EXPRESS and the ChoironeX phase 1 kidney trial, NCT07696962.
milestones.threshold_quote: Overall survival of the recipient without the need for chronic dialysis at Month 6.

milestones.title: FDA accepts a pig-organ biologics licence application as filed.
milestones.criterion: FDA receives all pertinent information and data and accepts the application as filed. Required material includes nonclinical and clinical evidence addressing safety, purity and potency, manufacturing methods, product stability, representative samples, test results and proposed labelling. This is the application-review gate before the separate licensing decision.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 601.2(a), applicable to biological products seeking licensure.
milestones.threshold_quote: shall not be considered as filed until all pertinent information and data have been received by the Food and Drug Administration.

milestones.title: A pig organ supplies life-supporting function in a nonhuman primate.
milestones.criterion: Transplant a genetically engineered pig organ into a nonhuman primate that depends on the graft for the function under study. Document recipient survival and measure graft function. For a kidney, removal of both native kidneys allows filtration to be attributed to the graft.
milestones.set_by: Life-supporting transplant convention used in pig-to-primate kidney and heart studies.

milestones.title: Initial kidney or heart trial recipients reach the protocol’s 12-week safety review.
milestones.criterion: In EXPAND and EXTEND, the independent data monitoring committee reviews safety and efficacy once the first six kidney recipients reach at least 12 weeks after transplant and decides whether the study should continue. In EXPRESS, the sponsor provides FDA with data after the first heart recipient reaches at least 12 weeks and before the second transplant.
milestones.set_by: United Therapeutics, published EXPAND, EXTEND and EXPRESS study designs.
milestones.threshold_quote: After all six participants reach at least 12 weeks post-transplant, safety and efficacy data will be reviewed by an Independent Data Monitoring Committee

not_found: No common numerical duration or survival-rate criterion for destination therapy across kidney, heart and liver was located in the FDA, IXA and ISHLT material searched.
No public numerical success margins for EXPAND or EXPRESS, completed pivotal cohort results, or filed pig-organ product BLA were located.
No published destination-therapy liver trial protocol was located.
The full 2026 ISHLT cardiac xenotransplantation consensus document could not be opened; its society landing page was accessible.
ClinicalTrials.gov returned its page shell without study details; the sponsor-submitted EXPAND record was readable through its ICH GCP mirror.

results.finding: 9 of 15 monkeys receiving engineered pig kidneys survived at least 3 months.
results.detail: The 60% survival rate meets the approximate proportion, but nine survivors fall short of the required 10. Survival beyond six months was demonstrated; the text does not establish that it was free of life-threatening immunosuppression complications.

results.finding: One living recipient of a gene-edited pig kidney became dialysis-independent, with sustained graft function through day 52.
results.detail: Intensified immunosuppression reversed T-cell-mediated rejection on day 8. Autopsy showed severe coronary artery disease and ventricular scarring without evident graft rejection.
results.quote: The xenograft functioned immediately. The patient's creatinine levels decreased promptly and progressively, and dialysis was no longer needed. After a T-cell-mediated rejection episode on day 8, intensified immunosuppression reversed rejection.

results.finding: Cynomolgus monkeys with HTG-D pig kidneys (n = 16) depended on their grafts for filtration, with the longest survival exceeding 2 years.
results.quote: xenograft survival with excellent kidney function beyond 1 year was achieved, with the longest survival exceeding 2 years

results.finding: In cynomolgus monkeys given EGEN-2784 pig kidneys (n = 16), six grafts failed within 25 days.
results.detail: The authors attributed the early losses to thrombotic microangiopathy.
results.quote: six out of 16 recipients in this group lost their xenograft early, within 25 days.

results.finding: Eight of 15 baboons survived more than one month with a functioning gene-edited pig heart.
results.quote: Eight of 15 baboons survived >1 month with a functioning xenograft.

results.finding: In the 15-baboon gene-edited pig heart series, median survival was 41 days.
results.detail: Survival after a switch to a baboon allograft was excluded when counting recipients who exceeded six months of pig-heart support.
results.quote: Median survival for the entire series was 41 days.

results.finding: Four baboons received genetically engineered pig liver grafts, with survival up to 29 days.
results.detail: The longest survivor maintained relatively normal liver tests for most of follow-up. Portal vein thrombosis was found at necropsy after euthanasia for bleeding plantar ulcers.
results.quote: Baboon # 4 was clinically well with stable LFTs until POD29, when euthanasia was again necessitated by plantar ulcerations as well as rising LFTs.

results.finding: Of four baboons receiving genetically engineered pig liver grafts, two had nearly one month of rejection-free survival.
results.detail: One early endpoint followed a seizure and the other followed worsening liver function. Cholestasis and bleeding plantar ulcers affected the longer survivors.
results.quote: Thus, nearly one-month rejection-free survival has been achieved following LXT in 2 of 4 continuous recipients

results.finding: Three of five EGEN-2784 kidney recipients remained dialysis-independent for more than eight months.
results.detail: The release reports the aggregate outcome and cites a Lancet publication for one recipient.
results.quote: Three of these patients have achieved sustained kidney function for more than eight months without the need for dialysis.

results.finding: eGenesis reports FDA clearance of the EGEN-2784 RESTORE kidney trial for 33 planned participants.
results.detail: The sponsor reports the clearance in a press release. The planned start was the first quarter of 2027.
results.quote: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared eGenesis to conduct a Phase 1/2/3 trial (RESTORE) to evaluate EGEN-2784 in 33 patients with kidney failure who are between 50 and 70 years of age and waitlisted for a human donor kidney transplant.

results.finding: An auxiliary pig liver showed hepatic activity in one living recipient and remained in place for 38 days.
results.detail: Xenotransplantation-associated thrombotic microangiopathy prompted graft removal. The 38 days measure time to explant. The patient died on day 171 after recurrent upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage.
results.quote: However, on postoperative day 38, the auxiliary liver was removed due to xenotransplantation-associated thrombotic microangiopathy (xTMA).

results.finding: Two EGEN-2784 kidney recipients were dialysis-free, with one sustaining dialysis independence for more than 7 months.
results.detail: Both recipients received the graft through expanded access.
results.quote: To see a patient thriving off dialysis for over seven months with a genetically engineered pig kidney is nothing short of groundbreaking,

results.finding: FDA reportedly cleared 1 EGEN-2784 kidney trial IND. The release gives no enrollment count.
results.detail: The sponsor announced the clearance in a press release.
results.quote: announced today that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared its Investigational New Drug (IND) application to initiate a clinical trial evaluating EGEN-2784, a genetically engineered porcine-derived kidney, in patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD).

results.finding: FDA cleared the UHeart EXPRESS trial under its IND, with up to 2 participants planned for the initial cohort.
results.detail: The sponsor's press release is the sole evidence provided for the FDA action.
results.quote:
has granted clearance under the company’s Investigational New Drug application to proceed with a clinical study of its investigational UHeart™ derived from a pig with 10 gene edits. The study, known as
EXPRESS
,
will enroll an initial cohort of up to two participants.

results.finding: One living recipient had initial circulatory support from a gene-edited pig heart before graft failure required ECMO on day 31.
results.detail: The recipient transitioned to comfort care after 40 days.
results.quote: Subsequently, the xenograft developed rapidly progressing diastolic heart failure, biventricular wall thickening and, ultimately, near-complete loss of systolic function necessitating initiation of extracorporeal membranous oxygenation on day 31.

results.finding: Six baboons received life-supporting genetically engineered pig kidneys, with median recipient survival of 261 days.
results.quote: Among all recipients, mean and median survival was 220 days and 261 days, respectively;

results.finding: Among six consecutive baboons receiving 10GE pig kidneys, four maintained graft function beyond six months.
results.detail: One graft failed hyperacutely. Among the five initially stable grafts, the study attributed two losses to rejection and associated three with adenovirus infection.
results.quote: Four of five low-risk recipients maintained graft function beyond six months

results.finding: Among 4 additional baboons given life-supporting pig heart grafts, 2 reached 3-month survival.
results.detail: Cardiac function remained within normal ranges throughout the long-term experiments.
results.quote: In 2 further experiments, PCMV infections were successfully avoided, and 3-months survival was achieved.

results.finding: Among 8 baboons given orthotopic pig heart grafts, 2 reached the 6-month survival threshold.
results.detail: Both recipients that reached 6 months came from the earlier series. In the four new experiments, the two long-term survivors reached 3 months and the other two died from porcine cytomegalovirus infection.
results.quote: Recently, we reported the stepwise optimization of pig-to-baboon orthotopic cardiac xenotransplantation finally resulting in consistent success, with 4 recipients surviving 90 (n = 2), 182, and 195 days.

results.finding: United Therapeutics reported FDA IND clearance for the UKidney trial, with 6 patients planned in the initial cohort.
results.detail: The clearance is reported in the sponsor’s press release.
results.quote:
today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug 
Administration (FDA) has cleared its Investigational New Drug application (IND) to initiate a clinical study of 
the company’s investigational UKidney™ derived from a 10 gene-edited source pig.

results.finding: Among 21 cynomolgus monkeys receiving engineered pig kidneys, the longest recipient survival was 758 days.
results.quote: renal grafts derived from the 3KO.7TG ± RI porcine donor supported life long-term in cynomolgus monkeys, up to 758 days.

results.finding: In 15 cynomolgus monkeys receiving engineered pig kidneys with human transgenes, median graft survival was 176 days.
results.detail: Maintenance immunosuppression varied among recipients. Thrombotic microangiopathy, with or without antibody-mediated rejection, was found in transgene-group recipients euthanized for renal failure.
results.quote: median survival time of 176 days versus 24 days

results.finding: Four baboons received life-supporting orthotopic transplants of ten-gene-edited pig hearts, with maximum survival of 225 days.
results.detail: Maintenance immunosuppression used mycophenolate and primatized anti-CD40. One recipient developed acute cellular rejection and another experienced ventricular fibrillation after progressive right ventricular outflow obstruction.
results.quote:
10 GE cardiac xenografts provide life-supporting function up to 225 days (mean
128 ± 36 days) in a non-human primate model.

results.finding: One living recipient (n=1) remained dialysis-independent for more than one year after receiving a genetically engineered pig kidney.
results.detail: Falco had been on dialysis since 2024 and received the kidney on November 22, 2025, under the FDA Expanded Access pathway.
results.quote: a patient with end stage kidney disease (ESKD) has become the first patient to surpass one year of dialysis independence following transplantation with a genetically engineered porcine kidney.

results.finding: A genetically modified pig heart sustained circulation without mechanical support in one living recipient for approximately 45 days.
results.detail: Sudden diastolic graft failure prompted ECMO restart on day 49. Life support was withdrawn on day 60.
results.quote: The patient was weaned from ECMO, and the xenograft functioned normally without apparent rejection. Sudden diastolic thickening and failure of the xenograft occurred on day 49 after transplantation, and life support was withdrawn on day 60.

results.finding: In one brain-deceased human recipient, an orthotopic pig liver graft continuously produced albumin and bile for 11 days.
results.detail: Microthrombosis impaired graft perfusion and likely contributed to late hepatic decline. Platelet counts fell and clotting factor activity declined.
results.quote: Throughout the 11-day observation period, the xenograft maintains continuous albumin and bile production with normal composition, albeit at a relatively low level.

results.finding: FDA cleared the IND for EGEN-5784 extracorporeal pig liver support in a Phase 1 trial with up to 20 planned participants.
results.detail: The release gives the announcement date. It leaves the FDA receipt date and the timing of clearance relative to the 30-day window unspecified.
results.quote: the U.S. Food & Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared the investigational new drug (IND) application for EGEN-5784, a human-compatible, genetically engineered porcine liver, used in combination with the OrganOx extracorporeal liver cross-circulation (ELC) system

definition = "A genetically engineered pig organ replaces the function of a failed human kidney, heart or liver as ongoing treatment. Xenotransplantation means transplantation between species. In destination therapy the pig organ is intended to sustain the recipient without a planned human transplant. An auxiliary liver graft can provide temporary support while the patient awaits recovery or a human liver.". Reason: The definition explains planned human replacement but leaves the distinction between full organ replacement and auxiliary liver support implicit.

goal.need = "On 30 July 2026, US waiting lists had 95,492 entries for a kidney, 8,776 for a liver and 4,039 for a heart. Some kidney candidates face years on dialysis and may die waiting. Pig donors could make transplantation possible when a suitable human organ is unavailable. For a kidney recipient, lasting graft function could mean years free from dialysis. Recipients would still need monitoring for infections that can pass from pigs to people.". Reason: Organ-specific counts show the scale of the shortage directly, and the revised text explains what another donor source would change for patients.

add statement by International Society for Heart and Lung Transplantation, 2026: "trial in ‘destination’ patients may be considered.". Reason: ISHLT explicitly identifies a cardiac trial in destination patients and states what must precede it.

add statement by RSPCA Australia, 2020: "RSPCA Australia is opposed to the use of animals for xenotransplantation.". Reason: The existing statements omit a published animal-welfare policy that directly opposes the use of animals for this purpose.

add milestone after None: "A pig organ supplies life-supporting function in a nonhuman primate.". Reason: The entry starts with a reproducibility benchmark and omits the earlier demonstration that one graft can supply life-supporting function.

edit m1: title = "Pig grafts show consistent, long-term function in an animal model relevant to the intended use."; criterion = "Prospectively assess long-term graft survival and safety in a series of animals using the intended clinical product and, where feasible, the clinical immunosuppression regimen and surgical procedure. Demonstrate stable, reproducible graft function. For hearts, ISHLT specifies at least 5\u201310 nonhuman primate models across multiple centres, each showing at least 6 months of survival with normal graft function on stable maintenance immunosuppression. FDA individualises the preclinical programme for each product."; set_by = "FDA describes the general design of definitive preclinical studies in its 2022 briefing document. ISHLT sets the numerical cardiac benchmark in its 2026 consensus perspective."; set_by_kind = "professional_society"; threshold_quote = "at least 5\u201310 non-human primate models across multiple centers, each demonstrating \u22656 months of survival"; threshold_ref = 29; refs = [5, 29, 9, 24]. Reason: The 2000 thoracic benchmark obscures FDA’s product-specific approach and ISHLT’s updated multicentre cardiac threshold.

edit m2: criterion = "Document an interval in which the transplanted organ supplies the function a living recipient needs. For a kidney, demonstrate renal function sufficient for independence from dialysis. For a heart, demonstrate circulation sustained by the graft without mechanical circulatory support. For a liver, demonstrate that the graft supplies the required hepatic function independently of the native liver. Record the duration of support."; set_by = "Clinical proof-of-concept convention. IXA identifies dialysis independence for kidneys and freedom from mechanical support for hearts, and distinguishes auxiliary liver support from definitive replacement."; refs = [2, 5, 11, 26, 27, 28]. Reason: The current criterion mixes individual outcomes with the test and gives no direct measure of the function attributable to each graft.

edit m3: criterion = "The investigational new drug application covering the prospective trial goes into effect 30 days after FDA receives it unless FDA notifies the sponsor of a clinical hold, or on earlier FDA notification that the clinical investigations may begin.". Reason: The criterion currently mixes the legal test for starting a trial with announcements of clearances and a first transplant.

add milestone after m3: "Initial kidney or heart trial recipients reach the protocol’s 12-week safety review.". Reason: The kidney and heart protocols specify an interim review before further enrolment that is separate from trial clearance and the later cohort assessment.
